extracted.intended_audience: inventors, applicants, and patent representatives seeking Eurasian (EAPO) patent protection
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for filing and prosecuting a Eurasian (EAPO) regional patent application, including documents required, timelines, examination stages, and subject‑matter eligibility. Geared toward applicants and their representatives who want protection across EAPO Contracting States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements (documents and parties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Full name and address of the applicant(s); Full name and address of inventor(s); Invention specification including claims, description, abstract and drawings; Certified copy of priority document if convention priority is claimed (can be claimed and filed within three months from the application filing date); International publication, international search report, international preliminary examination report for entry of PCT application into national phase; Simply signed Power of Attorney (POA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the mandatory elements to file a Eurasian Patent application at the Eurasian Patent Organization (EAPO). Note the certified copy of priority document may be submitted within three months of filing when priority is claimed. For PCT national/regional phase entry, include the international documents (publication, ISR, IPRP) as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of filing and translation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Eurasian application can be filed in ANY language with further submission of translation into Russian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may initially file in any language, but a Russian translation must be submitted subsequently (follow EAPO deadlines for translations). Filing in one language can reduce translation costs, but timely translation is required for prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The application undergoes formal examination within 2 months from the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal examination is the first procedural stage; positive formal results are required before substantive examination proceeds. Ensure all formal documents and POA are correctly submitted to avoid formal objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing and options
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent application is published after expiration of 18 months from the application filing date or priority date (if any). It may, however, be published earlier at the applicant's request upon payment of an additional fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication ordinarily occurs at 18 months but can be accelerated upon request and fee. Publication affords provisional protection between publication and grant within the scope of the published claims on the territory of all Contracting States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for substantive examination (deadline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for substantial examination can be filed within 6 months from the application publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive examination will only be conducted upon timely filing of this request (and payment of the official fee). For PCT-origin applications entering the regional phase, the substantive examination request must be filed within 6 months from publication of the PCT application or simultaneously with entering the regional phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of official fee for substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: On condition of payment of the Official Fee, the substantial examination is conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive examination is conditional on fee payment. Ensure the official fee is paid within the deadlines to trigger examination; otherwise prosecution will not proceed to substantive patentability analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant decision, registration fee, and issuance timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention meets the requirements of protectability the grant decision is issued. After payment of the registration fee the Final Decision to grant the Patent is issued within 2-4 months. Term for payment of the prescribed fee is 4 months from the date of issue of the Decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional 'Decision of the readiness to grant' is issued first; payment of the registration/registration fee leads to final grant. Observe the 4‑month payment term to secure grant; failure to pay may prevent issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall expected timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: The approximate timeframe of obtaining a patent is about 2-3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an approximate timeline from filing to grant under typical prosecution; actual timing depends on examination, responses, and payment promptness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paris Convention priority claim timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority under the Paris Convention should be claimed within 12 months from the filing date of the initial application. If for reasons beyond the applicant's control the application can not be filed within the specified time limit, an extension for two months may be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim priority within 12 months of the first filing. Where permitted, a 2‑month extension may be available for reasons beyond control—document and justify such reasons promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT regional phase entry time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limit for entry of PCT application into regional phase is 31 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using the PCT route, ensure entry into the Eurasian regional phase by 31 months from priority to avoid loss of regional rights. Substantive exam request deadlines (see above) may also apply on entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Contracting States and annuities
rubrics_metrics.description: In Eurasia it is not necessary to designate the Contracting States when filing the Eurasian Patent Application. The opportunity to designate the countries for the legal protection comes only when the Eurasian Patent is granted. If a patent owner does not pay a due annuity for a certain country, the patent becomes invalid on the territory of this country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation of which Contracting States will be covered occurs post‑grant. Annual fees (annuities) may be paid per designated state; non‑payment causes loss of protection in that state. EAPO offers a simplified procedure for paying annual fees across countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional protection after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The Publication of the Eurasian Patent Application affords provisional legal protection within the scope of the published claims on the territory of all the Contracting States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From publication until grant, the applicant has provisional protection limited to the published claims. Consider timing of enforcement or licensing decisions in that provisional window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects not patentable (excluded subject matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following objects are not patentable as inventions in Eurasia: Discoveries; Scientific theories and mathematical methods; Presentation of information; Business organization and management methods; Symbols, schedules and rules; Methods of performing mental acts; Computer programs and algorithms; Topographies of integrated circuits; Projects and plans for structures and buildings and for land development; Solutions concerning solely the outward appearance of manufactured goods and aimed at satisfying aesthetic requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are explicitly excluded from patentability under the Eurasian system. If an invention touches excluded subject matter, draft claims and disclosures to emphasize technical character and technical contribution to avoid exclusion where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional non‑grantable categories (public order / plant/animal varieties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eurasian Patents cannot be granted for plant or animal varieties; Invention, the commercial use of which it is essential to prevent for the purposes of protecting public order or morality, including the protection of the life and health of people and animals or the protection of plants, or in order to prevent serious damage being caused to the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if technically novel, inventions whose commercial use must be prevented to protect public order, morality, health, life or the environment are excluded. Note: prohibition cannot be based solely on whether one or more Contracting States law forbids the use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advantages / characteristics of the Eurasian regional system
rubrics_metrics.description: Eurasian patent system provides a uniform application procedure ... filing one application in one language, instead of filing the separate ones to the National Patent Offices; one representative for all steps during the procedure; one language that helps to reduce translation costs; one examination procedure that enables to save time and money; legal protection covering a large region with relative simplicity; after granting of the Patent it must not be validated by national authorities; simplified procedure of paying annual fees for every number of countries; obtaining a strong Eurasia Patent since all Eurasian applications have to undergo substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are practical benefits of using the EAPO route: centralized filing, prosecution, and fee payment can reduce cost and complexity compared to separate national filings. Use these features when advising clients on territorial strategy.
